I set up the library crate `platform_lib` in `/work`. It builds, its 2 tests pass, and clippy reports nothing on Linux. `cargo check` also passes for Windows, wasm32, macOS (aarch64) and FreeBSD.

**How the conditional-compilation code is kept readable:**

1. **Named aliases in `build.rs`** (using the `cfg_aliases` crate). Groups like `apple`, `linux_like` and `bsd` are defined once, so code says `#[cfg(apple)]` instead of repeating a long `any(target_os = "macos", ...)` list. Misspelled aliases still get a compiler warning.
2. **`cfg_if!` for chains of options.** When there are more than two mutually exclusive cases, an `if / else if / else` block replaces stacked `#[cfg]` attributes. The fallback case is written out explicitly.
3. **One file per platform in `src/sys/`.** There are four: `unix.rs`, `windows.rs`, `wasm.rs`, and `fallback.rs` for targets with no dedicated file. Each exposes the same items, and `src/sys/mod.rs` picks exactly one with a single `cfg_if!`. The public API in `src/lib.rs` has no `#[cfg]` at all.

```
Cargo.toml        # deps: cfg-if; build-deps: cfg_aliases
build.rs          # platform alias definitions
src/lib.rs        # public API + conventions documented in crate docs
src/sys/mod.rs    # backend selection
src/sys/{unix,windows,wasm,fallback}.rs
```

The public API (`os_family()`, `LINE_ENDING`, `config_dir_env()`) is placeholder code that shows the pattern; replace it with your real functionality. To support a new platform, add an alias in `build.rs`, a file in `src/sys/`, and one branch in `src/sys/mod.rs`.

To run those cross-target checks I installed four extra targets in your Rust toolchain via `rustup`. I haven't committed anything.
